chunks: Fourthly, this sect has become extinct. Not in our time, nor before us for a very long time, a believer of this creed has existed. If it were a true faith, its extinction would have been impossible.
ai.seo_question: What is the argument for the invalidity of the Kaisaniyya creed based on historical extinction?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi employs the principle of *istidlal bi'l-inqidar* (argument from extinction) to critique the Kaisaniyya, noting that the prolonged absence of any living proponent who genuinely held their specific doctrine serves as a divine indicator of its invalidity. This reflects the Shia scholarly view that truth, being from God, tends to persist or leave enduring traces, whereas false sects often fade when their specific claims lack divine support. The text underscores the historical reality that by Tusi's time, the distinct voice of the Kaisaniyya had effectively vanished, reinforcing their marginal status in Islamic theology. }
